etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French via Middle English and Middle French entreprise, feminine past participle of entreprendre (“to undertake”), from entre (“in between”) + prendre (“to take”), from Latin inter + prehendō, see prehensile.

definitions.definition: A company, business, organization, or other purposeful endeavor.
An undertaking, venture, or project, especially a daring and courageous one.
(uncountable) A willingness to undertake new or risky projects; energy and initiative.

quote.text: This loss of interest, hair, and enterprise — / Ah, if the game were poker, yes, / You might discard them, draw a full house! / But it's chess.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) Active participation in projects. (Can we add an example for this sense?)
(intransitive) To undertake an enterprise, or something hazardous or difficult.

quote.citation: 1733–1737, Alexander Pope, [Imitations of Horace], London:  […]  R[obert] Dodsley [et al.]:
quote.text: Charles Mordaunt Earl of Peterborow […] , with only 280 horse and 950 foot , enterprised and accomplished the Conquest of Valentia

definitions.definition: (transitive) To undertake; to begin and attempt to perform; to venture upon.

quote.citation: 1670, John Dryden, The Conquest of Granada:
quote.text: The business must be enterprised this night.

quote.citation: c. 1680, Thomas Otway, letter to Elizabeth Barry
quote.text: What would I not renounce or enterprise for you!

definitions.definition: (transitive) To treat with hospitality; to entertain.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book II, Canto II”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC, stanza 14:
quote.text: Him at the threshold met, and well did enterprize.
